plan: Gaps at 178: N&Q 2, Algebra 2, Functions 2, Geometry 2, S&P 1, IES 1; 5 hard / 4 medium / 1 easy. New subskills: complex modulus, units-digit cycles, absolute-value equations with an extraneous branch, parallel lines, sinusoidal model thresholds, exponential model from two points, polygon area by decomposition, interior angles, probability of independent unions, square-unit conversion.

candidates.stem: For i = √(−1), the absolute value of a complex number a + bi is √(a² + b²). What is the value of |3 − 4i| · |1 + i| ?

A.rationale: 5 is |3 − 4i| alone; it still must be multiplied by |1 + i| = √2.

C.rationale: This adds the parts of 3 − 4i as 3 + 4 = 7 instead of using the square root formula.

D.rationale: This takes |1 + i| as 2 (adding 1 + 1) instead of √2.

hints: Find each absolute value separately using the formula.
Multiply the two results.

candidates.stem: What is the units digit of 7¹⁰⁰ ?
candidates.explanation: The units digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of 4: 7¹ → 7, 7² → 9, 7³ → 3, 7⁴ → 1, then 7, 9, 3, 1 again. Since 100 is a multiple of 4, 7¹⁰⁰ has the same units digit as 7⁴, which is 1.

B.rationale: 3 is the units digit of 7³, the third term of the cycle; 100 leaves remainder 0 when divided by 4, which matches the 4th term.

C.rationale: This assumes every power of 7 ends in 7.

D.rationale: 9 is the units digit of 7², which would correspond to a remainder of 2.

hints: Find the units digits of 7, 7², 7³, 7⁴ and 7⁵.
Where does 100 fall in the repeating cycle?

strategy.explanation: Cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 of length 4; 100 ÷ 4 has remainder 0, so the digit is the last in the cycle: 1.

candidates.remember: Units digits of powers repeat; use the remainder.

author_checklist.dup_note: related to the powers-of-i cycle item (CLD-ACT-M-000069) but a different object

candidates.subskill: Absolute value equations with an extraneous branch
candidates.stem: What is the set of all real solutions of the equation |x − 4| = 2x + 1 ?
candidates.explanation: Case 1: x − 4 = 2x + 1 gives x = −5, but then the right side is 2(−5) + 1 = −9, and an absolute value cannot equal a negative number, so −5 is rejected. Case 2: −(x − 4) = 2x + 1 gives 4 − x = 2x + 1, so x = 1; check: |1 − 4| = 3 and 2(1) + 1 = 3. The only solution is x = 1.

B.rationale: −5 comes from the first case, but it makes the right side negative (−9), which an absolute value can never equal.

C.rationale: These are the solutions of both cases before checking; −5 is extraneous.

D.rationale: x = 1 does satisfy the equation, so the solution set is not empty.

hints: Split into the two cases x − 4 = 2x + 1 and x − 4 = −(2x + 1).
Check each result in the original equation; the right side must not be negative.
candidates.remember: If the other side has a variable, check for extraneous solutions.

author_checklist.hardness: case split plus rejection of an extraneous solution

candidates.stem: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, line m passes through the point (2, −1) and is parallel to the line 3x − y = 4. What is the x-intercept of line m ?
candidates.explanation: 3x − y = 4 can be written y = 3x − 4, with slope 3. Line m: y − (−1) = 3(x − 2), so y = 3x − 7. Setting y = 0: 3x = 7, x = 7/3.

A.rationale: −7 is the y-intercept of line m, not the x-intercept.

B.rationale: This uses the perpendicular slope −1/3 instead of the parallel slope.

D.rationale: 4 relates to the given line 3x − y = 4, not to line m.

hints: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
The x-intercept is where y = 0.

strategy.explanation: y = 3x − 7; set y = 0 to get x = 7/3.

candidates.remember: Parallel: same slope. x-intercept: set y = 0.

author_checklist.dup_note: the bank has a perpendicular-line item (CLD-ACT-M-000034) with y-intercept; this uses parallel lines and the x-intercept

candidates.subskill: Sinusoidal models: time above a threshold
candidates.stem: The water depth, in meters, at a pier t hours after midnight is modeled by h(t) = 3 sin(πt/6) + 5 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12. According to the model, for how many hours during this period is the depth greater than 6.5 meters?
candidates.explanation: h(t) > 6.5 means 3 sin(πt/6) > 1.5, so sin(πt/6) > 1/2. On 0 ≤ πt/6 ≤ 2π, sine exceeds 1/2 for π/6 < πt/6 < 5π/6, that is, 1 < t < 5. That is 4 hours.

A.rationale: This finds only the time from t = 1 to the peak at t = 3, forgetting the symmetric time after the peak.

C.rationale: 6 hours is the time the depth is above the midline, 5 meters (0 < t < 6), not above 6.5 meters.

D.rationale: This counts the time the depth is NOT above 6.5 m within the 12-hour period.

hints: Rewrite h(t) > 6.5 as an inequality about sin(πt/6).
For which angles between 0 and 2π is the sine greater than 1/2?

strategy.explanation: Sketch one period (12 hours) peaking at t = 3; the depth exceeds 6.5 between t = 1 and t = 5.

candidates.remember: sin θ > 1/2 for π/6 < θ < 5π/6 in one cycle.

author_checklist.hardness: unit-circle reasoning inside a model; symmetric-interval traps

candidates.stem: A population is modeled by P(t) = 200b^t, where t is in years and b is a positive constant. If P(3) = 1,600, what is the value of b ?

B.rationale: This divides 8 by 3 instead of taking the cube root.

C.rationale: This confuses the exponent 3 with the base b.

hints: Substitute t = 3 and P = 1,600.
After dividing by 200, take a cube root.
candidates.remember: Solve b^n = k with the nth root.

candidates.subskill: Area of a triangle by decomposition in the plane
candidates.stem: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, what is the area, in square units, of the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (5, 4) and (−2, 6) ?
candidates.explanation: Enclose the triangle in the rectangle from x = −2 to 5 and y = 1 to 6: area 7 × 5 = 35. Subtract the three right triangles around it: (1/2)(4)(3) = 6 [between (1, 1) and (5, 4)], (1/2)(7)(2) = 7 [between (5, 4) and (−2, 6)], and (1/2)(3)(5) = 7.5 [between (−2, 6) and (1, 1)]. Area = 35 − 20.5 = 14.5.

B.rationale: 20.5 is the total area of the three corner triangles that are cut away, not the triangle itself.

C.rationale: 29 is twice the area (the shoelace sum before halving).

D.rationale: 35 is the area of the enclosing rectangle.

hints: None of the sides is horizontal or vertical. Try enclosing the triangle in a rectangle.
Subtract the right triangles that lie inside the rectangle but outside the triangle.
candidates.remember: Slanted triangle: enclose in a box and subtract corners.

author_checklist.hardness: no side is on a grid line; requires decomposition
author_checklist.dup_note: the bank's altitude item (CLD-ACT-M-000073) has a side on the x-axis; this does not

candidates.stem: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
candidates.explanation: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon, (8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°, and each of the 8 equal angles is 1,080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

A.rationale: 108° is the interior angle of a regular pentagon.

B.rationale: 120° is the interior angle of a regular hexagon.

D.rationale: 140° is the interior angle of a regular nonagon (9 sides).

hints: How many triangles can an octagon be split into from one vertex?
Divide the angle sum by 8.

strategy.explanation: Exterior angle 360° ÷ 8 = 45°, so the interior angle is 180° − 45° = 135°.

candidates.stem: Events A and B are independent. P(A) = 0.4 and P(A or B) = 0.7. What is P(B) ?
candidates.explanation: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B), and for independent events P(A and B) = P(A)P(B). So 0.7 = 0.4 + p − 0.4p = 0.4 + 0.6p, giving 0.6p = 0.3 and p = 0.5.

A.rationale: 0.28 = 0.4 × 0.7 multiplies the two given probabilities, which is not P(B).

B.rationale: This subtracts 0.4 from 0.7, ignoring the overlap P(A and B).

D.rationale: This divides 0.3 by 0.4 instead of by 0.6.

hints: Write P(A or B) using the addition rule.
For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
candidates.remember: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

author_checklist.hardness: addition rule plus independence, solved backward

candidates.stem: A floor tile has an area of 2.5 square meters. What is its area in square centimeters? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
candidates.explanation: 1 square meter = 100 cm × 100 cm = 10,000 square centimeters. So 2.5 square meters = 2.5 × 10,000 = 25,000 square centimeters.

A.rationale: This multiplies by 100, converting as if the units were lengths, not areas.

B.rationale: This multiplies by 1,000, which is neither the length factor nor the area factor.

D.rationale: This multiplies by 100,000, one zero too many.

hints: How many square centimeters are in one square meter?
Square the length conversion factor.
candidates.remember: Area conversion uses the length factor squared.
